projects.title: Turion Hackathon 2025
projects.summary: A space-mission explorer that retrieves JPL Horizons data, plots trajectories, and experiments with mission summaries and a Three.js interface.
projects.why: Real astronomy data is difficult to approach. This prototype explores how a technical dataset can become a visual, searchable learning experience.
evidence: JPL Horizons vector requests and mission-range parsing
Matplotlib trajectory output plus a Flask workflow
A separate searchable Three.js mission explorer
projects.proof: Network-dependent flow still needs current end-to-end validation.

projects.title: HandwritingConverter
projects.summary: A local pipeline that turns photos of handwritten notes into a review report, searchable text, and a printable multipage PDF.
projects.why: Writing by hand can be the fastest way to think, but paper is hard to search and reuse. The tool connects those workflows without pretending handwriting OCR is perfect.
evidence: Image cleanup, confidence calculation, and local Tesseract OCR
Self-contained visual review output beside the transcription
Deterministic pytest coverage, Ruff checks, and CI
projects.proof: Recognition quality still depends on the page and installed OCR data.

projects.title: Ambient Dashboard
projects.summary: A retro desktop dashboard for priorities, progress, and focus sessions—designed to stay useful without becoming another noisy productivity system.
projects.why: Most dashboards ask for attention. This one explores the opposite: a small ambient surface that makes the day legible at a glance.
evidence: Reusable priority controls with local persistence
Focus timer, recent session history, and theme palettes
React/TypeScript production build inside a Tauri shell
projects.proof: Weather, calendar, automated tests, and packaging remain future work.

projects.title: Gesture-Reactive Avatar
projects.summary: A local webcam avatar that calibrates to a user, smooths expression changes, and maps facial landmarks to a library of cat reactions.
projects.why: The project treats computer vision as an interaction material—not just a prediction—and keeps camera processing on the local computer.
evidence: Rule-based eye, eyebrow, and mouth state combinations
Tests for calibration progress, reset, and initial smoothing
projects.proof: Camera behavior still needs broader face, lighting, and device testing.

projects.title: VoxNav
projects.summary: A voice-control assistant with an explicit command vocabulary for navigation, shortcuts, dictation, media, and allowlisted application launching.
projects.why: Hands-free control is useful only when the system is understandable and stoppable. VoxNav emphasizes visible decisions, safe previewing, and explicit commands.
evidence: Deterministic parser tests and safer subprocess launching
projects.proof: Live microphone, hotkey, and desktop control require intentional manual testing.

projects.title: Rose Hackathon 2026
projects.summary: A browser yoga-pose game that compares live landmarks with data-derived angle targets and returns joint-specific coaching, scores, and streaks.
projects.why: It explores a complete feedback loop: observe a pose, compare it with a target, explain the largest mismatch, and let the user try again.
evidence: MediaPipe inference and mirrored landmark canvas in the browser
FastAPI pose-data endpoint and static web delivery
CSV-to-pose conversion with target values and tolerances
projects.proof: Accuracy, camera recovery, and cross-device behavior still need real-device checks.
